brief.objective: Design a serving stack that runs a 7B-parameter open-weight LLM at a 32,768-token context window on a single NVIDIA A100 40 GB GPU, serving at least 8 concurrent requests.
constraints: One NVIDIA A100 GPU with 40 GB of HBM. All weights, KV cache, and activations must fit.
The 32k context window is a hard product requirement and cannot be reduced.
At least 8 concurrent requests must be served without preemption.
Target interactive latency: under 2 seconds time-to-first-token (TTFT).
topics: KV cache size: how many bytes per token, and how attention variants (MHA vs GQA vs MQA) change the budget.
Whether to quantize the KV cache or the weights, and the quality cost of doing so.
PagedAttention and continuous batching versus static batching.
Chunked prefill and prefill/decode scheduling to hold the TTFT target.
When to fall back to a shorter context plus retrieval instead of full 32k attention.
strict_notes: Use retrieved evidence for factual technical claims.
Cite exact sources and do not invent citations.
State uncertainty when the supplied evidence does not settle a claim.
Show the arithmetic for any memory budget claim.
